proposal.hypothesis: The selected two-target/128-thread candidate measured 0.002585 s, faster than the tested two-target/256-thread candidate at 0.002745 s, but both were slower than the 0.001844 s baseline. Test a 96-thread, 192-target mapping: it keeps two targets per thread and source-register reuse, while increasing the number of CTAs by one third versus the selected parent for a fixed N. Three warp-aligned warps per CTA may improve scheduling/resource distribution, but smaller CTAs may add overhead or reduce latency hiding. No speedup is assumed; all scored sizes and correctness cases should be checked by the controller.

retained: Set block=96, items_per_block=192, and shared_memory_bytes=0, maintaining exactly two targets per thread.
Map each lane to blockIdx.x*(2*blockDim.x)+threadIdx.x and that target plus blockDim.x; independently guard both targets in partial groups.
Load source position and mass once per source iteration and reuse them across both separate target accumulations in registers.
Write each valid target exactly once; use no shared-memory source tiling or block-level multi-output assignment.
